newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pakistan to seek less diesel, fuel oil for Jul-Sep.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to seek less diesel, fuel oil for Jul-Sep.

text.p: Pakistan is expected to buy up to 50 percent less fuel oil and diesel during July-September compared with its second quarter imports because of the monsoon season, an official with the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources said on Monday.
He said the tender for the third quarter is expected to be issued around May 15 and would close during the first week of June.

"We will buy less oil products than in the second quarter, maybe up to 50 percent lower," the official said. "This is because of excess hydropower during the monsoon season when demand for fuel oil from power plants falls drastically."
He said diesel imports would also drop because there is no demand from trucks amid a lull in sowing and harvesting activities.
"Diesel taken by power plants is also minimised," he said.
Pakistan bought a total of 450,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel in its last tender for April-June deliveries from Saudi-based trader Bakri Trading.
The award was between 84 cents and $1.14 per barrel above MidEast spot quotes, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Keamari.

It also bought 400,000 tonnes of 3.5-percent sulphur, 180-centistoke grade fuel oil from Bakri Trading and Sharjah Oil Refining Co and 300,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur fuel oil from Bakri Trading, Dutch trader Vitol and Swiss trader Glencore.

The 3.5-percent grade was awarded between $11.76 and $11.80 per tonne above MidEast quotes, c-and-f Fotco and the 1.0-percent sulphur grade was between $44 and $49.50 per tonne above MidEast quotes, c-and-f Keamari.
